name: Ketamine

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant human GluN1/GluN2A NMDA receptor (Xenopus oocytes)
recombinant human GluN1/GluN2A NMDA receptor (Xenopus oocytes)
recombinant mu-opioid receptor expressed in CHO cells (CHO-mu)
recombinant kappa-opioid receptor expressed in CHO cells (CHO-kappa)

functional.cell_system: HEK293 expressing HCN1; cortical pyramidal neurons

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Acute: blocks open NMDA channel (use-dependent, voltage-sensitive). Disinhibits cortical pyramidal cells via preferential blockade of GABAergic interneuron NMDARs → glutamate surge → AMPA activation → BDNF/TrkB → mTORC1 → synaptogenesis (Duman/Aghajanian model). HCN1 inhibition contributes to hypnosis. The major active metabolite (2R,6R)-HNK potentiates AMPA via α7 nAChR-dependent presynaptic mechanism (Marcantoni 2024, doi:10.1038/s41398-024-02744-y).

neuroimaging.finding: Acute ketamine increases prefrontal/ACC BOLD signal and decreases default-mode network connectivity in humans; matches subjective dissociation
Acute ketamine increases gamma power (30-80 Hz), decreases alpha power; biomarker of dissociation and rapid antidepressant response
[11C]-(+)-PHNO displacement studies show ketamine increases striatal dopamine release ~20% at subanesthetic doses (consistent with ~3% D2/D3 occupancy by displaced DA)

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Oral ketamine AUC increased ~2.6× by clarithromycin (strong CYP3A4 inhibitor)
Inhibits norketamine formation; increases ketamine AUC

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6 516 G>T carriers showed roughly 2.4-fold higher oral esketamine plasma levels than non-carriers (median 5.1 vs 2.1 ug/L, p=0.032) in a small treatment-resistant-depression sample (n=18); no significant effect was seen on metabolite levels, or for CYP3A4*22 or CYP3A5*3.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Rapid tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing (hours to days); use-dependence of NMDA blockade reduces with sustained channel blockade
cross_tolerance: DXM (partial, via different NMDA site kinetics)
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild compared to opioids/benzos. Onset 24-72h after cessation in heavy users: craving, dysphoria, anhedonia, fatigue, GI distress. Lasts 1-2 weeks. Urinary tract symptoms (ketamine cystitis) may persist months.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Contributes to hypnotic action; HCN1 KO mice resistant to ketamine anesthesia
Minor at clinical concentrations; indirect sympathomimetic effects dominate cardiovascular profile
Inhibition at supratherapeutic doses; not clinically dominant
Ulcerative cystitis in chronic high-dose users (>1 g/day); norketamine implicated as direct urothelial toxin

demographic_differences.sex: Women have slightly lower CL/F and higher peak exposure on weight-normalized basis
demographic_differences.age: Pediatric CL/kg higher than adult; elderly show decreased CL
demographic_differences.weight: Standard weight-based dosing; obese patients may need lean-body-weight calculation
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment reduces CL significantly; renal impairment minor effect on parent but HNK glucuronides accumulate

data_gaps_remaining: definitive μ-opioid functional agonism vs allosteric modulation; mechanism of urothelial toxicity

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant mu-opioid receptor expressed in CHO cells (CHO-mu)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same as racemic ketamine but ~2× more potent. FDA approval (Spravato 2019) for TRD relies on NMDA-mediated disinhibition + downstream synaptogenesis.

neuroimaging.finding: Spravato 84 mg intranasal increases ACC and PFC activation, decreases DMN connectivity in TRD patients

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6 PMs show higher esketamine exposure; clinical dose adjustment not specified by Spravato label

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Tachyphylaxis with frequent dosing; Spravato dosing is twice-weekly induction then weekly/biweekly
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Similar to ketamine; not formally characterized for esketamine alone

demographic_differences.age: Elderly (≥65): clearance reduced; dose adjustment per label
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Moderate hepatic impairment: AUC ↑ ~58%; severe hepatic impairment not studied

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: See Esketamine record.

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant mu-opioid receptor expressed in CHO cells (CHO-mu)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hashimoto group has consistently shown R-ketamine produces longer-lasting (>1 week) antidepressant-like effects in rodents than S-ketamine despite lower NMDA affinity. Mechanism proposed: σ1 agonism + sustained BDNF-TrkB-mTOR signalling + ERK pathway in mPFC. Phase 2a (Perception Neuroscience PCN-101) failed primary endpoint May 2023 but showed signal at 60 mg without dissociation.

neuroimaging.finding: (R)-ketamine produces distinctly different theta power changes vs (S)-ketamine — possibly tied to differential σ1 engagement

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6 PMs likely show larger exposure increases for arketamine than esketamine because CYP3A4 contribution is smaller

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Lower dissociation than esketamine; abuse potential likely lower

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same use-dependent NMDA channel block as parent. Higher norketamine/ketamine ratio with oral route makes norketamine a major active species in oral ketamine PD.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Proposed primary mediator of ketamine cystitis in chronic users

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Proposed mechanism (Zanos/Gould): presynaptic α7-nAChR activation → glutamate release → AMPA potentiation → BDNF → TrkB → mTOR → synaptogenesis WITHOUT NMDA blockade or dissociation. This decoupling drove HNK as a non-dissociative antidepressant candidate (Phase 1 NIH 2023).

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Predicted minimal (no NMDA blockade, no dissociation)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Strong NMDA channel block + indirect dopaminergic effects via σ-receptor-mediated DA release modulation in NAc (Nishikawa 1999, doi:10.1016/S0014-2999(99)00769-4).

neuroimaging.modality: phMRI (relative cerebral blood volume), anesthetized rat
neuroimaging.finding: PCP (0.5 mg/kg i.v.) produces robust, sustained rCBV increases across cortico-limbo-thalamic regions, the circuit signature used as a model of NMDAR-hypofunction schizophrenia; clozapine abolishes the thalamic component while raclopride has no effect

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Tolerance develops to subjective effects within days of repeated use
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Heavy chronic users: anxiety, depression, craving, weight loss, sleep disturbance; psychotic symptoms may persist weeks

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Highly lipophilic → enterohepatic recycling; gastric lavage useful in overdose

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Most NMDA-potent compound in the class. Combination of high-affinity NMDA blockade + σ1 agonism + SERT inhibition may explain unique agitation/mania/psychosis profile distinct from ketamine, MXE.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Rapid tolerance; users often escalate to maintain effects
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Psychological dependence; agitation/psychosis on cessation in heavy users

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: NMDA blockade dominant; SERT inhibition contributes serotonergic component that may underlie the longer-duration and 'antidepressant-like' subjective profile vs ketamine.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Marketed as 'bladder friendly' but unsubstantiated: 3 months of dosing in mice produced bladder inflammation and fibrosis plus tubular and glomerular renal damage, similar to comparable chronic-ketamine models.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same compound as DMXE record.
Behaves as ketamine pharmacologically. Longer duration than ketamine likely due to slower phase-I metabolism (the 2-chlorine in ketamine accelerates CYP-mediated oxidation).

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Heavy users report craving, anxiety, dysphoria

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Similar to 3-MeO-PCP profile but with N-ethyl on a cyclohexylamine scaffold (vs piperidine). Reported as more 'stimulating' than MXE.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Reports of mania, agitation similar to 3-MeO-PCP

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Deschloro-N-ethyl analogue of ketamine. Predicted similar potency to MXE without the 3-MeO group.
See O-PCE.
Pure DAT inhibitor with cocaine-like behavioral profile (Le Foll 2000 Neuropsychopharmacology) but binds at a DAT site allosterically distinct from cocaine.
Thiophene-2 in place of phenyl ring. Functional in vivo profile similar to ketamine — used as Telazol (with zolazepam) in veterinary anesthesia.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Plasma t½ varies by species: cat 2.4 h, dog 1.2 h, monkey 1-1.5 h (pmid:17083465)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: N-methyl analogue of tiletamine (vs N-ethyl). No published pharmacology.
Slightly less potent than PCP per behavioral studies; less stimulant character.
See 3-MeO-PCE record (with lowercase 'e' in input list duplicate).
Meta-fluoro analogue of PCP. No published Ki. By SAR analogy to 3-MeO-PCP (very high NMDA affinity 20 nM) and 3-F bioisostere logic — expected NMDA Ki 30-100 nM range.
See 3-Fluoro-PCP.
Ethoxy analogue of 3-MeO-PCP. Expected slight reduction in NMDA affinity vs methoxy (bulkier group in the 3-position). No published Ki.

Morpholine analogue. The PCMo series (Wallach 2017 ACS Chem Neurosci doi:10.1021/acschemneuro.7b00269) showed 3-MeO morpholine analogues retain NMDA affinity but lower than the piperidine counterpart.
N-propyl analogue of 3-MeO-PCE. Higher lipophilicity may extend duration.
Pyrrolidine + 3-MeO analogue. No published Ki.

By structural analogy to 3-HO-PCP, expected to combine NMDA antagonism + μ-opioid agonism. 3-HO-PCP MOR Ki 39-60 nM, KOR Ki 140 nM (Itzhak 1985). The 3-OH PCE analogue likely shares this profile but no formal data.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Possible opioid-like withdrawal in addition to NMDA-class withdrawal

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Br-for-Cl bioisostere of ketamine. Expected slightly higher NMDA affinity than ketamine (larger halogen, more lipophilic) but no formal binding data published.
See 2-Bromodeschloroketamine.

By definition this name is identical to ketamine itself (ketamine = 2-chlorophenyl). The name 'deschloroketamine' refers to removal of chloro, so '2-chlorodeschloroketamine' is contradictory; likely a market naming artifact for ketamine.
Fluoro-substituted analogue of FXE (3-F-2-oxo-PCE). No published binding data.

Ortho-methoxy analogue of ketamine. Methoxy in 2-position replacing chloro. No published Ki; expected NMDA affinity similar to or slightly lower than ketamine because the ortho-methoxy may sterically interfere with PCP-site binding.
See 2-MeO-Ketamine.

Methylenedioxy in 3,4-position. No published binding data. Methylenedioxy substitution often introduces 5-HT2/SERT activity in other drug classes (MDMA vs methamphetamine) — possible additional serotonergic component vs PCP.
N-allyl analogue of ketamine. Allyl groups often produce CYP-suicide-inhibition; PK consequences possible.
N-cyclobutyl analogue of ketamine. No published binding data.
N-cyclopropyl analogue of ketamine. Cyclopropyl is a common 'metabolic stability' substitution.
N,N-dimethyl analogue of ketamine. N,N-dialkyl substitution generally reduces NMDA affinity in the arylcyclohexylamine series — expected lower potency than parent ketamine.
Han 2019: N-ethyl-norketamine series acts via AMPA + 5-HT2 pathway, similar to (2R,6R)-HNK proposed mechanism, but with retained NMDA activity.
See Ethketamine.
Fluorinated MXE analogue. Subjective duration reported shorter than MXE.
2-fluoro analogue of O-PCE / N-ethyl-2F-DCK. Expected NMDA affinity similar to or higher than ketamine, by analogy to 2F-DCK.
3-OH analogue of MXE. By analogy to 3-HO-PCP (μ-opioid Ki 39-60 nM) — likely μ-opioid agonist + NMDA antagonist. Could be hazardous combination.
N,N-dialkyl ketamine analogue. Expected lower NMDA affinity than parent ketamine.
N,N-dialkyl ketamine. No data.
N-isopropyl analogue of MXE. Expected NMDA Ki similar to or slightly lower than MXE.

3-MeO-2'-oxo-PCP. Combines the 3-MeO substitution of 3-MeO-PCP with the 2'-oxo of ketamine — predicted highest NMDA affinity in the class per the task brief class context ('2'-Oxo + 3-MeO hits the highest affinity'). No published Ki.
N-propyl analogue of MXE. Expected similar pharmacology to MXE.
Deschloro-nor-ketamine — primary amine (no N-substituent). NH2 is the simplest variant; expected lower NMDA affinity than secondary amines.
N-allyl deschloroketamine. Allyl group may trigger CYP suicide inhibition.
N-(2-hydroxyethyl) analogue. Polar N-substituent may decrease BBB penetration.

2'-oxo (ketone) analogue of PCP. The β-keto group restricts conformation similar to ketamine. By Abelian 2024 SAR analysis, 2'-oxo substitution shifts subjective profile toward 'heavier/holier' character vs non-keto PCP — possibly via preferential occupation of one of the two PCP-site binding poses (Zhang 2021).
N-propyl analogue of ketamine. SAR generally shows N-methyl > N-ethyl > N-propyl at NMDA, so likely lower potency than parent.

class_name: Arylcyclohexylamines (NMDA antagonists at the PCP binding site)
shared_mechanism: Arylcyclohexylamines are use-dependent, voltage-sensitive, non-competitive blockers of the NMDA receptor channel at the PCP binding site within the central vestibule. Channel block requires the channel to be open (agonist-bound, depolarized). Cryo-EM structures of S-ketamine bound to GluN1/GluN2A and GluN1/GluN2B (Zhang 2021, doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03769-9) revealed two distinct sub-poses within the binding pocket, mediated primarily by hydrophobic and hydrogen-bond interactions with GluN2A-L642 (≡ GluN2B-L643) and GluN1-N616. The two-pose model rationalizes apparent SAR discrepancies. Beyond NMDA blockade, members of the class engage σ1 receptors (PCP, 3-MeO-PCP strongly; ketamine weakly), serotonin and other monoamine transporters (MXE family especially SERT; 3-MeO-PCP SERT; PCP weakly DAT), HCN1 channels (ketamine, anesthetic relevance), and μ/κ-opioid receptors (3-HO-PCP strongly; ketamine weakly — debated as functional contributor to antidepressant action). The major ketamine metabolite (2R,6R)-hydroxynorketamine does NOT block NMDA at antidepressant-relevant concentrations and instead acts via α7-nAChR-dependent presynaptic glutamate release plus AMPA potentiation (Marcantoni 2024, Suzuki 2017).
shared_pk_summary: Hepatic CYP-mediated metabolism dominates the class. Ketamine cleared predominantly by CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 to norketamine (active, 3× less potent at NMDA), then to (2R,6R)-HNK and dehydronorketamine. Oral routes give norketamine >> parent drug due to first-pass (norketamine/ketamine plasma ratio ~6:1). Bioavailability: IV 100%, IM ~93%, intranasal 25-50%, sublingual ~25-30%, oral ~17-25%. Half-lives 2-4 h for ketamine class; PCP is an outlier at 1-3 days due to high lipophilicity. Protein binding 12-50% across the class. CYP2B6*6/*6 PMs show ~50% reduction in oral ketamine clearance with implications for TRD therapy.
shared_safety: Acute risk: respiratory depression at high doses (potentiated when combined with opioids or alcohol). Cardiovascular sympathomimetic effects (HR/BP increase). Emergence delirium, dissociation, occasional violent psychomotor agitation (highest for 3-MeO-PCP, 3-MeO-PCE, PCP). Hepatic toxicity — case reports for some research chemicals. Chronic risk: ulcerative cystitis (norketamine implicated) in heavy daily users; cognitive impairment; psychological dependence. Key off-targets: HCN1 (ketamine hypnosis), σ1 (3-MeO-PCP psychosis profile), μ-opioid (3-HO-PCP/E respiratory depression). Fatal blood concentrations: PCP >200 ng/mL, 3-MeO-PCP 50-3,525 ng/mL (very narrow window), ketamine >1,000 ng/mL (very wide therapeutic index).
sar_summary: Core scaffold: phenyl + cyclohexyl + amine. SAR principles, with primary literature: (1) Aryl ring substitution dominates NMDA affinity: 3-methoxy > 3-ethoxy > 3-methyl > 3-fluoro > H > 2-chloro (ketamine); 4-position less effective than 3-position (Roth 2013 doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0059334). (2) 2'-oxo (β-keto) substitution: shortens duration, restricts conformation, shifts pose preference at PCP site (Zhang 2021), produces 'heavier' subjective profile per Abelian 2024 SAR analysis. (3) N-amine: N-methyl (ketamine) > N-ethyl (MXE/O-PCE) > N-propyl > N-cyclopropyl; primary amine (norketamine) ~3× less potent than N-methyl. Piperidine (PCP) and pyrrolidine (rolicyclidine) typically more potent at NMDA than secondary amines but with different σ1 and PK profiles. (4) Combining 2'-oxo + 3-MeO + piperidine (MXPCP-like) predicted maximum NMDA affinity. (5) Aryl ring replacement: thiophene-2 (tiletamine) retains NMDA activity; benzothiophene-2 (BTCP) eliminates NMDA and switches to DAT-selective. (6) Meta-OH (3-HO-PCP/E series) introduces μ-opioid agonism alongside NMDA blockade — major safety implication.
